correctness.rationale: For a weighted simple connected graph |V|>=3, separate each third vertex's two incident weights and use convexity of the absolute-distance sum to prove a sharp local gain theta|w_uz-w_vz||f(u)-f(v)|. The edge uv contributes -2 min(theta,1-theta) w_uv, and independent selection of remaining vertex levels attains the sum. Discrete coarea/layer cake reduces the induced J_w norm modulo constants to characteristic cuts; their explicit gains give the cut formula, and positive cut weight plus vertex modular costs yield a standard u-v min-cut threshold for k>=1. Unit-weight tree and multipartite subclasses follow from neighborhood degrees. Independently calculated exactly all cuts for 30 random rational weighted graphs at each n=3,4,5,6 and verified optimal sharp gain and inequalities; this is bounded corroboration, not the general proof.
